questions.question: For n approaching infinity, what is the tight asymptotic class of 3n^2+7n+2?
questions.explanation: The quadratic term dominates. Positive constant factors and lower-degree terms do not change the tight asymptotic class.

questions.question: For eventually positive functions f and g, which condition is equivalent to f(n)=Theta(g(n))?

options.B: f=O(g) but f is not Omega(g)
options.C: f=Omega(g) but f is not O(g)
options.D: f is neither O(g) nor Omega(g)

questions.explanation: Theta is the intersection of constant-factor upper and lower bounds. The other options each explicitly omit at least one of those necessary bounds, so the four conditions are disjoint.

questions.question: Two phases always execute sequentially: the first takes Theta(n log n) time and the second Theta(n^2). What is their combined tight time complexity?
questions.explanation: Sequential costs add. Since n^2 grows faster than n log n, their sum is Theta(n^2), rather than the product of the phase costs.

questions.question: Python 3 (analysis). Assuming unit-cost integer operations, what is the tight running time as positive n grows?
questions.explanation: The inner body executes 1+2+...+n=n(n+1)/2 times. The loop overhead does not change the quadratic bound.

questions.question: Python 3 (analysis). For n=2^k, k>=0, what is the tight number of iterations? Treat arithmetic as unit cost.
questions.explanation: The positive values are n,n/2,...,1, giving k+1 iterations. For asymptotically growing n, this is Theta(log n).

questions.question: For powers of two, T(1)=1 and T(n)=2T(n/2)+1. What is the tight solution?
questions.explanation: The recursion tree is a full binary tree with n leaves and 2n-1 total nodes. Each node costs constant time; this is also Master Theorem case 1.

questions.question: For powers of two, T(1)=1 and T(n)=T(n/2)+1. What is the tight solution?
questions.explanation: There is one recursive subproblem at each halving level. The depth is log2(n), with constant local work per level.

questions.question: For powers of two, T(1)=1 and T(n)=2T(n/2)+n. What is the tight solution?
questions.explanation: Every nonleaf level costs n, and there are log2(n) such levels. The leaves add Theta(n), yielding Theta(n log n).

questions.question: A recursive function calls itself on n-1 until zero and stores only a constant number of machine words per live call. There is no tail-call elimination. Excluding input/output storage, what is its peak recursion-stack space?
questions.explanation: All n+1 call frames can be live before unwinding. Constant-size frames multiplied by linear depth give Theta(n) stack space.

questions.question: Which list is in strictly increasing asymptotic growth order as n tends to infinity? All logarithms have fixed base greater than one.

options.A: sqrt(n), log n, n, n log n
options.B: log n, sqrt(n), n, n log n
options.C: n log n, n, sqrt(n), log n
options.D: log n, n, sqrt(n), n log n

questions.explanation: Any positive power of n eventually dominates log n; sqrt(n) grows slower than n, and n log n grows faster than n.

questions.question: For positive integer n tending to infinity, which statement correctly distinguishes an upper bound from a tight bound?

options.D: n is O(n^2), but n is not Theta(n^2)

questions.explanation: A valid upper bound need not be tight. n<=n^2 establishes O(n^2), but n/n^2 tends to zero, ruling out a quadratic lower bound.

questions.question: For powers of two, T(1)=1 and T(n)=4T(n/2)+n. What is the tight solution?
questions.explanation: n^(log2 4)=n^2 dominates the linear nonrecursive term by a polynomial factor. Master Theorem case 1 therefore gives Theta(n^2).

questions.question: For powers of two, T(1)=1 and T(n)=2T(n/2)+n^2. Which tight solution follows, including the case-3 regularity check?

options.B: Theta(n^3), because branch count multiplies every root cost
options.C: Theta(n^2 log n), because every level costs n^2

questions.explanation: The nonrecursive term is polynomially larger than n. The child local-work sum is one-half the parent term, satisfying regularity and forming a decreasing geometric series.

questions.question: For powers of two, T(1)=1 and T(n)=2T(n/2)+n log2(n). Using the generalized equal-branch Master Theorem for nonnegative log powers, what is T(n)?
questions.explanation: The critical polynomial is n and f=n log n. The equal-power case adds one logarithmic factor; a recursion-tree sum also gives n times 1+2+...+log2(n).

questions.question: For powers of three, T(1)=1 and T(n)=3T(n/3)+n. What is the tight solution?
questions.explanation: The total local work is n at every branching level and there are log3(n) levels. The logarithm base changes only a constant factor.

questions.question: For powers of three, T(1)=1 and T(n)=9T(n/3)+n^2. What is the tight solution?
questions.explanation: The branching critical power is n^(log3 9)=n^2, matching f. Each level contributes Theta(n^2), adding a logarithmic factor.

questions.question: For integer n>=1, T(0)=1 and T(n)=T(n-1)+n. Which tight solution and method are correct?

options.A: Theta(n log n) by setting b=1 in the standard Master Theorem
options.B: Theta(2^n) because the depth is n
options.C: Theta(n^2) by summing the decreasing linear costs
options.D: Theta(n) because there is one recursive call

questions.explanation: Expansion gives 1+sum(i, i=1..n), a quadratic sum. The standard divide-by-constant Master Theorem requires b>1 and does not directly apply to n-1.

questions.question: A function has T(n)=T(n-1)+Theta(1), stops at zero, and uses constant-size frames without tail-call optimization. What are its tight time and peak stack bounds?

options.C: Time Theta(log n), stack Theta(log n)

questions.explanation: There are linearly many calls, each with constant local work. All frames remain live at the deepest call, so both time and stack grow linearly.

questions.question: Python 3 (analysis). What is the tight running time? All arithmetic and each body update cost one unit.
questions.explanation: The inner loop runs floor(n/i) times. Summing over i gives the harmonic sum n H_n up to linear rounding error, hence Theta(n log n).

questions.question: Python 3 (analysis). For n a positive power of two, what is the tight running time under unit-cost operations?
questions.explanation: The body counts 1+2+4+...+n=2n-1. Multiplying the maximum inner length by the number of outer iterations would overestimate this geometric sum.

questions.question: Python 3 (analysis). For n>=2 tending to infinity, what is the tight number of loop iterations? Ignore the bit cost of integer multiplication.
questions.explanation: After j updates, i=2^(2^j). Crossing n therefore requires j proportional to log2(log2(n)), not log2(n).

questions.question: Let T(n)=T(n/2)+T(n/4)+n for powers of two, with positive constant base cases for n<=2. What is its tight solution?
questions.explanation: The sum of subproblem sizes contracts by a factor 3/4 per level, bounding total nonrecursive work by a geometric series O(n). Root work alone supplies Omega(n).

questions.question: Python 3 (analysis). Calls execute sequentially; each frame uses Theta(1) auxiliary words and no tail-call elimination is performed. What is the peak recursion-stack space?
questions.explanation: Peak stack is one active root-to-leaf path, not all recursion-tree nodes at once. The two branches execute sequentially, so depth is logarithmic.

questions.question: A recursive algorithm allocates an n-word local buffer, retains it until return, and then recursively processes two n/2 subproblems sequentially. Each child follows the same rule. Excluding input/output and assuming powers of two, what is peak auxiliary space?
questions.explanation: On one active path, live buffers total n+n/2+n/4+...<2n. The second child reuses time after the first is finished; cumulative allocation across every call is not peak live space.

questions.question: As n approaches infinity, how does (log2 n)^10 compare with n^0.01?

options.C: They are Theta of each other
options.D: Their ratio alternates forever between zero and infinity

questions.explanation: Any fixed positive polynomial power eventually dominates any fixed power of a logarithm. Large constant exponents can delay that crossover but do not change the asymptotic relation.

questions.question: For real n>1, simplify n^(1/log2 n) and identify its tight growth class.

options.B: It equals n and is Theta(n)
options.D: It equals log2 n and is Theta(log n)

questions.explanation: Writing n=2^x gives (2^x)^(1/x)=2. The specified logarithm base fixes the constant; the expression does not grow with n.

questions.question: A dynamic array starts at capacity one and doubles capacity whenever an append finds it full. A resize copies all existing elements, and an ordinary append costs one unit. Over n appends, what are the tight total and amortized-per-append costs?

options.D: Total Theta(n log n), amortized Theta(log n)

questions.explanation: Copied counts form 1+2+4+... below 2n, and the n appends themselves cost n. Thus all operations together cost Theta(n), although an individual resizing append may cost Theta(n).

questions.question: For powers of two, T(1)=1 and T(n)=4T(n/2)+n^2 log2 n. What is the tight solution?
questions.explanation: The critical polynomial is n^2. Multiplying it by one logarithm in the nonrecursive work gives an additional logarithm in the generalized equal-power case.

questions.question: For powers of two n>=4, T(n)=2T(n/2)+n/log2 n, with T(2)=1. What is the tight solution? Do not assume a Master-Theorem case that requires a nonnegative log exponent.
questions.explanation: Set n=2^k and S(k)=T(2^k)/2^k. Then S(k)=S(k-1)+1/k, so S(k)=Theta(log k). Multiplying by n gives Theta(n log log n); the negative log power is a boundary case.

questions.question: For inputs divisible as needed, consider T(n)=T(n/3)+T(2n/3)+n with positive constant base cases and ordinary rounding that does not change asymptotics. What is its tight complexity?
questions.explanation: The child sizes sum to the parent size. There are logarithmically many full-cost levels before the shallowest leaves, giving Omega(n log n); maximum logarithmic depth and per-level cost at most n give the matching upper bound.

questions.question: A recurrence is T(n)=T(sqrt(n))+1 for n=2^(2^k), with T(2)=1. What is the tight solution as n grows?
questions.explanation: One square-root step reduces k by one because sqrt(2^(2^k))=2^(2^(k-1)). There are k=log2(log2 n) nontrivial steps.

questions.question: For n=2^k, define f(n)=n^2 when k is even and f(n)=4n^2 when k is odd. T(n)=2T(n/2)+f(n), with T(1)=1. Which assessment is correct?

options.A: The direct case-3 regularity test fails, but a recursion-tree bound still gives Theta(n^2)
options.B: Case 3 directly applies because 2f(n/2)<=f(n)/2 for every n
options.C: The recurrence has no asymptotic upper bound
options.D: Failure of regularity proves T(n)=Theta(n^2 log n)

questions.explanation: For even k, 2f(n/2)/f(n)=2, violating any eventual regularity factor below one. Nevertheless n^2<=f(n)<=4n^2, and level costs are bounded by a decreasing geometric series times n^2.

questions.question: For powers of two n>=4, T(n)=2T(n/2)+n/(log2 n)^2, with T(2)=1. What is the tight solution?
questions.explanation: With S(k)=T(2^k)/2^k, the increments are 1/k^2. Their sum is bounded, while the positive leaf contribution remains constant in S. Thus T(n)=Theta(n), rather than the extra log-log factor from 1/k.

questions.question: A pathological dynamic array increases capacity by exactly one whenever full, copying all existing elements. Starting empty with capacity one, perform n appends. What is the tight total cost and amortized cost per append?

options.C: Total Theta(n log n), amortized Theta(log n)

questions.explanation: Copies total 1+2+...+(n-1)=Theta(n^2). Adding n ordinary writes does not change that bound. Dividing by n gives linear amortized cost, unlike multiplicative capacity growth.

questions.question: For powers of two, T(n)=T(n/2)+T(n/4)+sqrt(n), with T(1)=T(2)=1. Let phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2. What is the tight solution?
questions.explanation: Writing n=2^k gives a Fibonacci-style homogeneous recurrence with growth phi^k. Its forcing term (sqrt(2))^k grows strictly slower than phi^k, so T(2^k)=Theta(phi^k), equivalent to the stated power of n.

questions.question: Python 3. What is printed? Dictionaries named nxt/prv represent node next/previous pointers; None is a null pointer. Node labels identify nodes, not implicit array positions.

def walk(nxt, head):
    out = []

nxt={1:2,2:3,3:4,4:None}

nxt={0:1,1:2,2:3,3:4,4:None}

Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What return value does this recursive greatest-common-divisor function print?
questions.explanation: The argument pairs are (84,30),(30,24),(24,6),(6,0). The base returns 6.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What is printed when a reference-free local is incremented after the recursive return?
questions.explanation: Unwinding adds the incremented local arguments 2,3,4. Their sum is 9; caller arguments are independent.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What is printed when the second recursive branch is skipped by a returned-value test?
questions.explanation: f(2)=2. Thereafter the a>=2 branch returns a+1, giving f(3)=3,f(4)=4,f(5)=5 without a second call at those levels.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What result and base-leaf count are printed for unequal branches?
questions.explanation: Leaf totals satisfy L(n)=L(n-1)+L(n-2) with L(0)=L(-1)=1, yielding L(1)=2,L(2)=3,L(3)=5. Each leaf returns one.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What result and final global value follow the left-to-right branching mutations?
questions.explanation: The first n=1 subtree returns 13 with g=5. After adding 2, the second subtree returns 31 with g=11. The root adds 13+31+11=55.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What result follows static mutation both before descent and after return?
questions.explanation: Descent raises s to 7. Unwinding increments it to 8,9,10 and accumulates 7+8+9+10=34. The next base call observes 10.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What sequence and final global value follow sibling calls with restoration?
questions.explanation: The first n=1 subtree prints 3 then 2; restoration removes the root contribution before the second subtree prints 1 then 0. All contributions are restored to zero.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What is printed when a static counter is shared across all tree nodes and a later root call?
questions.explanation: The first tree visits seven nodes with serials 1 through 7, summing to 28. The second visits serials 8,9,10 and returns 27.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What result and global value are printed when one call uses a global-derived argument?
questions.explanation: The first n=1 frame reaches g=5 before its parity-selected call. That nested n=1 frame returns 16 with g=9, so the first frame returns 20. At the root, g increments to 10, selecting a base call that returns 11. The root returns 31.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What result is printed when the same local snapshot is used around two recursive calls?
questions.explanation: The left n=1 frame saves 1 and returns 1+2+3=6. The right saves 3 and returns 3+4+5=12. The root adds its saved 1, giving 19.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What maximum frame count and total entries are printed for this mixed decrement recursion?
questions.explanation: The deepest path is 7,5,3,1,-1, containing five frames. Counting both branches and base entries by C(n)=1+C(n-2)+C(n-3) for positive n gives 17 entries.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What value is printed by this nested recursive return argument?
questions.explanation: f(9) calls f(11)=10, then f(10), which calls f(12)=11 and f(11)=10. Including the initial call gives five entries.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What sequence is printed when a static value changes between pre- and post-recursion output?
questions.explanation: Entries save mine=1,2,3. The base prints 3,3; unwinding adds saved 2 then 1 to the shared s, producing 5 and 6. A later base call increments s to 7.

questions.question: Typed pseudocode uses signed 32-bit Integer values, pass-by-value parameters, left-to-right evaluation, and div truncating toward zero. Globals and Static locals persist across calls; ordinary locals are fresh. Print appends space-separated tokens. What result and final global value follow this three-stage recursive mutation?
questions.explanation: The left subtree saves before=3 and returns 5 with g=3. The root subtracts its saved 1, leaving g=2; the right subtree returns 4 with g=3. The root then returns 5-4+3=4.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Which cloud service model gives a customer virtual machines on which it manages the guest operating system and its applications?

options.D: A deployment model called private cloud

questions.explanation: IaaS exposes computing infrastructure and leaves guest software administration with the customer.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A team deploys application source to a provider-managed runtime without administering the underlying operating system. Which service model best matches this capability?
questions.explanation: PaaS hosts customer applications while the provider operates the underlying runtime platform and infrastructure.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Employees use a provider-operated online payroll application and configure only tenant settings. Which service model is illustrated?

options.C: Hardware virtualization as a deployment model

questions.explanation: The capability consumed is the finished provider application, which makes it SaaS.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Which deployment model reserves a cloud infrastructure for one organization, even if a third party operates it off premises?

options.D: A public cloud made private merely by a login page

questions.explanation: Exclusive organizational use defines a private cloud. Its physical location and operator need not be the organization's own premises and staff.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A hypervisor runs directly on physical hardware rather than as an application on a conventional host operating system. What is its classification?
questions.explanation: A Type 1 hypervisor operates at the hardware virtualization layer; a Type 2 hypervisor runs on a host OS.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Which component do ordinary Linux containers on one Linux host share?

options.A: One mandatory root filesystem shared without isolation
options.B: A single process identifier shared by all container processes
options.C: One mandatory guest kernel per container

questions.explanation: Containers isolate processes and resources while sharing the host kernel. Their filesystems and process views can be isolated.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Which action is vertical scaling of a single server?

options.A: Removing idle servers after demand falls
options.B: Deploying the same-sized server in another region
options.C: Changing it from 4 vCPUs and 8 GiB RAM to 8 vCPUs and 16 GiB RAM
options.D: Adding four identical servers behind a load balancer

questions.explanation: Vertical scaling changes the resources of an individual machine; adding instances is horizontal scaling.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A service automatically adds instances during a traffic spike and removes them afterward. Which capability is most directly demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Elasticity adjusts provisioned capacity outward and inward with demand. Here automation performs both adjustments.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: For a conventional IaaS virtual machine, which task normally remains with the customer under shared responsibility?

options.A: Replacing failed physical server power supplies
options.C: Securing physical access to the provider data center
options.D: Applying security patches to the guest operating system

questions.explanation: The provider handles physical infrastructure and virtualization. Customers administer guest operating systems and their installed software.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A retailer retains a private cloud and connects it to a public cloud so applications can burst into the public capacity during peaks. Which deployment description is most precise?

options.A: Hybrid cloud with application portability between distinct clouds
options.B: Private cloud only, because a private component exists
options.D: Public cloud only, because peak capacity is public

questions.explanation: The integrated private and public infrastructures remain distinct while supporting workload portability, which fits hybrid cloud.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A company independently runs analytics on public provider A and email on public provider B. It has no private cloud or integrated portability layer. Which description fits the stated facts?

options.B: Multi-cloud use of two public providers

questions.explanation: Multi-cloud refers to using multiple cloud providers. The scenario supplies no private-cloud component or integrated hybrid arrangement.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A legacy application requires a customer-installed kernel module that its managed application platform prohibits. Which move gives the needed guest-kernel control with provider-managed physical hardware?

options.A: Move it to a SaaS tenant setting
options.B: Run it in an IaaS virtual machine with a compatible guest OS
options.C: Change only the application's DNS name
options.D: Put the same module in an ordinary unprivileged container on that prohibited platform

questions.explanation: IaaS allows control of the guest operating system, subject to virtual hardware support. Tenant settings and an unprivileged container do not grant prohibited kernel access.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A SaaS tenant accidentally grants all employees access to confidential payroll records through its own role configuration. Which statement best assigns responsibility for that configuration?

options.A: The hypervisor vendor must change the payroll permissions
options.B: The customer must correct its tenant access policy
options.C: The provider is automatically responsible for every customer-selected role
options.D: SaaS eliminates the need for identity and access administration

questions.explanation: Consuming SaaS reduces infrastructure work but does not eliminate customer responsibility for tenant identities, role choices, and data access.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A managed platform patches its OS and runtime, but a customer deploys an application with an SQL injection flaw. Under the stated boundary, who must fix the application code?

options.B: Only the data-center physical security team
options.D: Nobody, because PaaS prevents application defects

questions.explanation: The provider operates the platform; application logic remains customer-controlled. Managed runtime maintenance does not repair customer business logic.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A developer runs a desktop virtualization program as an application on an existing laptop OS, then installs a guest OS inside it. Which layer is the virtualization program?

options.B: A SaaS application runtime by definition
options.C: A Type 1 hypervisor running directly on bare metal

questions.explanation: A hosted virtualization program runs above a conventional host OS, matching Type 2 virtualization.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A deployment must run a Linux application and an application requiring a Windows kernel simultaneously on one physical server. Which design directly supplies the distinct kernels?

options.A: Two ordinary Linux containers sharing one Linux kernel
options.B: Two directory trees on one Linux host without virtualization
options.C: Separate Linux and Windows guest VMs on a suitable hypervisor
options.D: Two processes in the same Linux container namespace

questions.explanation: Separate VMs can boot distinct guest kernels. Ordinary containers share their host kernel and do not themselves turn a Linux kernel into a Windows kernel.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: An application stores session state only in each server's RAM. Traffic is randomly balanced to newly added servers without affinity. What directly addresses the resulting lost sessions during horizontal scaling?

options.A: Move session state to a shared service accessible to all application instances
options.B: Keep adding servers while assuming all instance RAM is shared
options.C: Use a larger logo on the login page
options.D: Double only the number of independent in-memory session copies without synchronization

questions.explanation: New instances do not inherit another process's memory. A shared session service allows every instance to retrieve the same session state; that dependency needs its own availability design.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: An autoscaling group reaches its configured maximum of ten instances while demand keeps rising. Which conclusion is justified?

options.A: Elastic growth is currently constrained by the configured capacity limit
options.B: Cloud elasticity guarantees unlimited usable capacity despite every limit
options.C: Every request must now succeed because autoscaling is enabled
options.D: The deployment has automatically become a private cloud

questions.explanation: Configured maxima, service quotas, and available resources bound real scaling. Enabling an autoscaler does not remove those constraints.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Two container replicas run on one host. The design must survive that host's complete failure. Which change directly removes this shared host dependency for the replicas?

options.A: Assign both containers more CPU on the same host
options.B: Give both existing containers different names
options.C: Place replicas on separate hosts and route traffic to healthy replicas
options.D: Add a third container on the same host

questions.explanation: Failure-domain separation is required: every container on a failed host loses that host. Independent hosts and health-aware routing address the specified failure.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A provider supplies an exclusively allocated cloud to one company from the provider's data center. The company says it cannot be private because it is off premises. Which correction is accurate?

options.A: Private clouds must be operated only by the customer's employees
options.B: Private-cloud classification depends on exclusive organizational use, not an on-premises requirement
options.C: Any off-premises cloud is necessarily public
options.D: Exclusive allocation always means the service must be SaaS

questions.explanation: A private cloud may be operated by a third party and located off premises; exclusive organizational use is the relevant deployment characteristic.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A service can be manually expanded from two to twenty instances, but stays at twenty when demand drops unless an operator intervenes. What does the scenario directly establish?

options.A: It is automatically elastic in both directions
options.B: It is horizontally scalable; automatic scale-in has not been demonstrated
options.C: It cannot be scalable because scaling is manual
options.D: It must use vertical scaling only

questions.explanation: Scalability is the ability to accommodate growth by adding capacity. The described manual process does not establish automatic demand-following contraction.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: An application provider meters storage and request counts and reports them to each tenant. Which cloud characteristic is most directly illustrated?

options.A: A prohibition on customer usage visibility
options.B: Dedicated physical hardware for every tenant
options.D: A requirement that every resource be free

questions.explanation: Metering and reporting consumption provide usage transparency. They do not imply a particular deployment model or pricing level.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A small web application needs only a supported managed runtime and must avoid routine guest-OS administration. Which choice best fits that requirement among the options?

options.A: An on-premises server with a manually maintained OS
options.C: IaaS VMs managed entirely by the application team
options.D: A desktop Type 2 hypervisor maintained by the application team

questions.explanation: The managed runtime satisfies the application need while delegating underlying OS maintenance. The other choices keep that administration with the team.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A disaster-recovery design copies a VM image nightly but keeps the only current database on the original host's local disk. The host and disk fail together. What gap most directly prevents recovery of recent application data?

options.A: The design has no surviving copy of the current database state
options.B: Virtualization automatically preserves every write after disk loss
options.C: The VM image contains too many operating-system files
options.D: Using a private IP address guarantees database durability

questions.explanation: A VM image is not a substitute for current database backups or replication. Recovery requires database state stored outside the failed disk's failure domain.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Three independent availability zones must serve 450 requests/second immediately after loss of any one zone. Each instance serves at most 100 requests/second; instances are distributed equally, traffic can rebalance perfectly, and no new instances can start during failover. What is the minimum deployment?
questions.explanation: With k instances per zone, two surviving zones supply 200k requests/second. 200k>=450 requires k=3; k=2 supplies only 400.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A three-voter service requires a majority of two live voters. It must retain a majority after any single availability-zone failure. Which placement meets this requirement?

options.A: One voter in each of three independent zones
options.B: Two voters in zone A and one in zone B
options.C: One voter in zone A and two in zone B
options.D: All three voters in one zone

questions.explanation: Spreading one voter across each of three zones leaves two after any one-zone loss. A 2+1 placement loses its majority if the two-voter zone fails.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: An API is duplicated across two public clouds, but every request in both clouds synchronously requires one shared identity endpoint. That endpoint fails completely and cached credentials are not accepted. What follows?

options.A: Exactly one cloud must remain able to authenticate every request
options.B: The API copies automatically remove the authentication requirement
options.C: Both API deployments can become unusable despite their separate clouds
options.D: Multi-cloud deployment makes the shared endpoint failure impossible

questions.explanation: Provider diversity does not remove an application-level shared dependency. The explicitly required identity endpoint is a common point of failure.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Two interchangeable application instances each have availability 0.99. The application tier works if either is available. Every request also needs a database with availability 0.999. All three component failures are independent, and routing has no failures. What is total availability?
questions.explanation: The application tier availability is 1-(0.01)^2=0.9999. Multiplying by 0.999 for the required database gives 0.9989001, or 99.89001%.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A workload jumps immediately to 900 requests/second. New instances take five minutes to become ready, and neither queuing nor request rejection is allowed. Each warm instance handles at most 150 requests/second. Warm instances must be split equally across three zones and still handle the spike after any one-zone loss. How many warm instances are minimally needed before the spike?
questions.explanation: If k warm instances occupy each zone, loss of one leaves 2k*150 capacity. Meeting 900 requires k>=3. Slow scale-out cannot supply capacity immediately.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Two replicas of a critical VM have automated restart, but both reside on one physical host and use one local disk. A proposed design must survive destruction of that host and disk without losing acknowledged writes. Which option addresses both stated requirements?

options.A: Use asynchronous nightly copies on the same local disk
options.B: Increase the one host's CPU count and restart the same VMs
options.C: Add more VM replicas on the same host and local disk
options.D: Use separate hosts and storage failure domains, synchronously replicate acknowledged writes, and provide health-based failover

questions.explanation: Host separation supplies surviving execution capacity; synchronous durable replication outside the failed storage domain preserves acknowledged writes. Failover must route to the surviving copy.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: In a conventional sequential Waterfall lifecycle, which ordering places the listed activities in their usual dependency order?
questions.explanation: The sequential model establishes requirements before design, builds from the design, and verifies the implementation afterward. Real projects may revisit phases.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Which development approach most directly supports delivering small increments and revising plans using frequent stakeholder feedback?

options.A: One irreversible requirements freeze followed by a single final delivery
options.C: Replacing all working software with planning documents
options.D: Skipping stakeholder review until after all maintenance ends

questions.explanation: Agile approaches use short feedback cycles and increments to adapt work as understanding changes.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: According to the Scrum Guide 2020, what is the primary purpose of the Daily Scrum?

options.A: Obtain mandatory daily task approval from a project manager
options.B: Formally accept the entire final product
options.C: Inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as needed

questions.explanation: The Daily Scrum helps Developers inspect progress and adapt their plan for the Sprint Goal; it is not primarily a management status meeting.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Which Scrum event focuses on inspecting the Sprint outcome with stakeholders and adapting what to do next?
questions.explanation: The Review inspects the product outcome and future adaptations. The Retrospective focuses on improving the team's effectiveness and quality.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Which Scrum event specifically plans improvements to quality and effectiveness by examining how the previous Sprint went?

options.D: Product Backlog refinement as a required formal event

questions.explanation: The Retrospective examines the team's interactions, processes, tools, and practices to identify improvements.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: In Scrum Guide 2020 terminology, which commitment belongs to the Product Backlog?

options.D: A mandatory fixed scope for every future Sprint

questions.explanation: The Product Goal is the Product Backlog commitment. The Sprint Goal and Definition of Done belong to the Sprint Backlog and Increment respectively.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Without -a or explicit path arguments, what does git commit normally use as the tracked-file snapshot for the new commit?

options.A: Every current working-tree file, including untracked files
options.B: Only files that have never been added to the index
options.C: The current index, also called the staging area
options.D: Only the latest remote branch contents

questions.explanation: A normal commit records the staged snapshot. Unstaged working-tree edits and untracked files are not included automatically.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: On main with a clean working tree, what does git branch feature do?

options.A: Copy the entire remote repository into a new directory
options.B: Create feature and immediately switch to it
options.C: Merge main into every existing local branch
options.D: Create feature at the current commit while leaving main checked out

questions.explanation: git branch creates a branch reference. Switching requires a separate command such as git switch feature.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: In the normal attached state on branch main, what does HEAD usually reference symbolically?

options.B: The oldest commit object in the repository
options.D: The index file as a branch name

questions.explanation: Attached HEAD refers symbolically to the current local branch, whose reference identifies its tip commit.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Initially, tracked file f.txt contains A in HEAD, index, and working tree. After the shown steps, which contents are committed and which remain in the working tree? Assume hooks make no changes.
questions.code_snippet:
edit f.txt to B
git add f.txt
edit f.txt to C
git commit -m "save staged version"

options.A: Commit contains B; working tree contains B
options.B: Commit contains A; working tree contains C
options.C: Commit contains B; working tree contains C
options.D: Commit contains C; working tree contains C

questions.explanation: git add copies B into the index. The later edit to C is unstaged, so commit records B while leaving the working tree at C.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: The graph is A--B--C, with main at A and feature at C. With a clean worktree, what does git switch main followed by git merge --ff-only feature do?

options.B: Create a two-parent commit after C
options.C: Move main to C without creating a new merge commit
options.D: Refuse because fast-forward always requires divergent history

questions.explanation: A is an ancestor of C, so a fast-forward advances only main's reference. No merge commit is needed.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: main and feature both descend from A with distinct new commits M and F. Their changes do not conflict. On main, what does git merge --no-ff feature create?

options.A: No commit, because divergent branches can only fast-forward
options.B: A rewritten F whose parent is M, deleting the original F object
options.C: A detached HEAD at A with unchanged branch references
options.D: A merge commit with first parent M and second parent F

questions.explanation: A non-fast-forward merge joins the two histories. On main, its current tip M is the first parent and the merged tip F is the second.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: During an ordinary two-branch merge, config.txt has conflict markers. A developer edits it to the desired combined content. Which sequence normally finishes the merge?

options.A: git stash drop, then git fetch
options.B: git rebase --continue without an active rebase
options.C: git branch config.txt, then git status
options.D: git add config.txt, then git commit

questions.explanation: Editing resolves the working file, but the index must also be marked resolved with git add. Committing then records the merge resolution.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A clean repository is modified in tracked t.txt and also gains an untracked notes.txt. Neither path is ignored. What does git stash push normally save and remove from the working tree?

options.A: Only notes.txt, leaving tracked edits in place
options.B: Neither file unless a remote is configured
options.C: Both files, because untracked files are always included
options.D: Tracked-file changes only; notes.txt remains untracked in the working tree

questions.explanation: Default stash includes tracked changes. Untracked files require an option such as -u; ignored files need additional inclusion.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A stash entry applies cleanly. Which difference between git stash apply and git stash pop is correct?

options.B: apply keeps the stash entry; successful pop removes it
options.C: apply removes the entry; successful pop keeps it
options.D: Both always remove every stash entry

questions.explanation: apply restores changes while retaining the entry. pop drops the applied entry on success; a conflict prevents its automatic removal.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A developer checked out an old commit directly, created new commit X in detached HEAD, and has not switched away. Which command creates and checks out a branch preserving X as its tip?

options.B: git switch main followed by git reset --hard main

questions.explanation: A new branch created at the current detached commit records X as a named tip and attaches HEAD to that branch.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A feature branch has commits F1 then F2, each adding a different independent file. main lacks both. On main, git cherry-pick F2 succeeds. Which changes are introduced?

options.A: Both F1 and F2 automatically, because cherry-pick copies all ancestors
options.B: F2's patch only, recorded as a new commit on main
options.C: No change until feature is merged
options.D: F2 replaces main's entire history with feature's history

questions.explanation: Cherry-pick applies the selected commit's change relative to its parent. It does not automatically replay ancestor patches; independence makes this application succeed.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A--M is main and A--F--G is feature. F and G have nonempty independent changes that are absent from M, and there are no conflicts. On feature, git rebase main uses the usual replay behavior. What history results?

options.A: A--F--G--M, with main moved to G
options.B: A two-parent merge commit joining M and G
options.C: A--M only, with both feature patches necessarily discarded
options.D: A--M--F'--G', with feature at G' and main still at M

questions.explanation: Rebase replays the feature commits on the new base. Their changed parentage yields new commit identities; main is not advanced by rebasing feature.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Two developers add unrelated files on branches that diverged from A. The branches are otherwise clean. Which statement about combining them is accurate?

options.A: A merge cannot retain both files without renaming both branches
options.B: Every divergent history necessarily produces conflict markers
options.C: Divergence alone does not imply a content conflict; Git can merge both additions
options.D: A rebase is guaranteed to preserve the original commit IDs

questions.explanation: Conflicts depend on incompatible changes, not simply on having two branch tips. Independent additions can merge automatically.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A Scrum team has a usable Increment meeting its Definition of Done halfway through a Sprint. Must it wait for the Sprint Review to release that Increment?

options.A: No; Scrum does not make the Sprint Review a release gate
options.B: No; but releasing automatically cancels the Sprint
options.C: Yes; every Increment must wait until the following Sprint
options.D: Yes; release is prohibited until the final project ends

questions.explanation: A Done Increment can be delivered before the Sprint ends. The Review is an inspection and adaptation event rather than a mandatory release gate.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A selected backlog item is coded but fails the Definition of Done. Under Scrum Guide 2020, which treatment is correct?

options.A: Release it as Done if the Sprint timebox expires
options.B: Count it as a Done Increment because coding finished
options.C: It is not part of the Increment and returns to the Product Backlog for future consideration
options.D: Automatically extend the Sprint until it is Done

questions.explanation: Work must meet the Definition of Done to be part of the Increment. An unfinished item cannot gain Done status merely through the Sprint ending.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Mid-Sprint, Developers and the Product Owner learn that a different implementation can better meet the same Sprint Goal. Which action is consistent with Scrum?

options.A: Lower the Definition of Done solely to report more completed items
options.B: Negotiate Sprint Backlog scope while preserving the Sprint Goal and quality
options.C: Automatically cancel the Sprint whenever any task estimate changes
options.D: Prohibit every change to the implementation plan after Sprint Planning

questions.explanation: The plan can adapt as more is learned. Scope may be renegotiated with the Product Owner without endangering the Sprint Goal or reducing quality.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A Sprint Goal has become obsolete. Who has the authority to cancel the Sprint under Scrum Guide 2020?

options.C: Only the Developers acting without the Product Owner

questions.explanation: The Product Owner has cancellation authority when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete. Estimates or individual task delays do not automatically require cancellation.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A team in a sequential Waterfall process discovers during system testing that a documented requirement was misunderstood. Which response best preserves traceability of the correction?

options.A: Review and update the affected requirement, design, implementation, and tests through change control
options.B: Change only the test expected result to match the faulty implementation
options.C: Delete the requirement without recording the reason
options.D: Treat discovery during testing as proof that requirements cannot be changed

questions.explanation: A requirement correction can affect several downstream artifacts. Coordinated change control keeps them consistent and records why they changed.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Starting clean on main, a normal merge of feature stops on a same-line conflict in f.txt. The three versions are shown. What are index stages 2 and 3 before resolution, and where does git merge --abort leave main?
questions.code_snippet:
Base A: f.txt = base
main at M: f.txt = main
feature at F: f.txt = feature
git switch main
git merge feature
# merge conflicts; inspect git show :2:f.txt and git show :3:f.txt
git merge --abort

options.A: Stage 2 is feature; stage 3 is main; abort advances main to F
options.B: Stage 2 is main; stage 3 is feature; abort restores main at M
options.C: Stage 2 is base; stage 3 is main; abort creates a merge commit
options.D: Stage 2 is main; stage 3 is base; abort deletes both branch refs

questions.explanation: During a normal merge, stage 2 is ours, the current branch, and stage 3 is theirs, the incoming branch. With the initially clean state, abort restores the pre-merge state at M.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Starting clean on feature, git rebase main stops while replaying its single nonempty commit F because both sides changed f.txt. main has independent file main.txt; F also adds extra.txt. If the developer selects git checkout --ours -- f.txt, stages f.txt, and successfully continues, what is retained?
questions.code_snippet:
A--M  main
 \--F feature
A: f.txt = base
M: f.txt = main; adds main.txt
F: f.txt = feature; adds extra.txt
git switch feature
git rebase main
git checkout --ours -- f.txt
git add f.txt
git rebase --continue

options.A: f.txt uses main's version; extra.txt remains; feature's replayed commit has main as parent
options.B: f.txt uses base content; feature is left at the original F
options.C: f.txt uses main's version; every nonconflicting change from F is necessarily discarded
options.D: f.txt uses feature's version; extra.txt disappears; main is rewritten

questions.explanation: During rebase, ours is the upstream plus commits already replayed. Selecting it for one path does not discard F's other staged changes. extra.txt keeps the replay nonempty.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Commits B, C, and D respectively add independent files b.txt, c.txt, and d.txt. M adds m.txt. All changes are nonempty and conflict-free. What does the shown rebase retain on feature?
questions.code_snippet:
A--M       main
 \--B--C--D feature
git rebase --onto main B feature

options.A: Only D' on A; m.txt and c.txt are absent
options.B: Original B, C, D remain unchanged and main moves to D
options.C: M, then new C' and D'; files m.txt, c.txt, d.txt are present and b.txt is absent
options.D: M, then new B', C', D'; all four files are present

questions.explanation: With --onto main B feature, commits after B reachable from feature are replayed onto main. B itself is excluded; independent C and D patches do not bring b.txt along.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: HEAD has f.txt=A. A developer stages B, then leaves C unstaged, stashes, restores with --index, and commits. All operations succeed cleanly and hooks make no edits. What state remains?
questions.code_snippet:
edit f.txt to B
git add f.txt
edit f.txt to C
git stash push
git stash apply --index
git commit -m "staged only"

options.A: Commit contains C; working tree contains C; stash entry is removed
options.B: Commit contains A; working tree contains B; stash entry remains
options.C: Commit contains B; working tree contains B; stash entry is removed
options.D: Commit contains B; working tree contains C; stash entry remains

questions.explanation: The stash stores both index B and working content C. apply --index restores that distinction and keeps the stash entry, so commit records B with C still unstaged.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: From a clean main at M, git cherry-pick C D successfully commits C' but then stops on a conflict while applying D. The developer immediately runs git cherry-pick --abort. What happens?

options.A: main advances to D even though its conflict was unresolved
options.B: main stays at C' because abort cancels only the current patch
options.C: main becomes detached at the original source commit C
options.D: main and tracked files return to their pre-sequence state at M, removing C' from the branch history

questions.explanation: Aborting the in-progress multi-commit cherry-pick sequence restores the state before the sequence began. --quit would only forget sequencer state and is a different operation.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Use two independent copies of the same clean graph. In copy 1, feature merges main with --no-ff. In copy 2, feature rebases onto main. F and G have nonempty, independent changes absent from M; all operations succeed. Which comparison is correct?
questions.code_snippet:
A--M    main
 \--F--G feature
Copy 1: git switch feature; git merge --no-ff main
Copy 2: git switch feature; git rebase main

options.A: Both operations necessarily create exactly one two-parent merge commit
options.B: Rebase leaves the original G as the tip because file content alone fixes commit identity
options.C: Merge retains original F and G as ancestors of its two-parent tip; rebase creates F' and G' after M and need not retain original F or G as ancestors
options.D: Merge rewrites F and G while rebase preserves all original parent links

questions.explanation: Merge joins the existing histories and keeps their original commits. Rebase changes feature parentage by replaying patches, producing new commit identities and a linear tip for this graph.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: In the conventional Linux filesystem hierarchy, which path primarily contains host-specific system configuration?
questions.explanation: /etc holds host configuration. /proc exposes virtual kernel/process information, /tmp holds temporary files, and /dev contains device nodes.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: On Linux with procfs mounted, what does /proc primarily expose?

options.A: Persistent user documents stored on a normal disk filesystem
options.B: A backup copy of every deleted file
options.C: Only executable binaries installed by users
options.D: A virtual interface to process and kernel information

questions.explanation: procfs is generated by the kernel and exposes system and per-process information; it is not an ordinary persistent document directory.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: What is the traditional role of /bin in the Linux filesystem hierarchy, including systems where it is implemented as a symlink into /usr/bin?

options.C: Storing per-process virtual memory maps only
options.D: Storing each user's private home directory

questions.explanation: /bin conventionally exposes essential command binaries. A merged-/usr implementation may supply that path through a symlink.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: For an ordinary file with no special permission bits, which symbolic permissions correspond to chmod 640 file?
questions.explanation: Owner digit 6 means read+write; group digit 4 means read; other digit 0 grants nothing.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Which command changes the owner of report.txt to alice, assuming the caller has the necessary privilege?
questions.explanation: chown changes ownership. chmod changes mode bits, while umask controls permissions removed at creation.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Which command prints lines in app.log containing the case-sensitive text ERROR?
questions.explanation: grep selects matching text lines. The other commands manage permissions, signals, and ownership.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: On a Linux system using a conventional ps implementation, what does ps -e request?

options.A: Continuous printing of every file in /etc
options.C: Only a list of currently open network ports

questions.explanation: The -e option selects all processes for ps output. ps reports a snapshot rather than sending signals.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: With no signal option, what signal does the conventional Linux kill command request for a specified process?
questions.explanation: The default request is SIGTERM, which a process can handle or ignore. SIGKILL requires an explicit signal selection and cannot be caught.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A normal file begins with mode 750. After chmod u-x,g+w file, what is its octal mode? Assume no ACLs or special bits.
questions.explanation: Owner 7 loses execute bit 1, becoming 6. Group 5 gains write bit 2, becoming 7. Others remain 0.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: With umask 027 and no default ACLs, a program requests a new regular file with mode 0666 and a new directory with mode 0777. What modes result?
questions.explanation: Creation permissions are requested_mode AND NOT umask, restricted to permission bits. This clears group write and all other permissions; it is not decimal subtraction.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A non-root user bob owns a regular file with mode 0460 and belongs to its owning group. Ignore ACLs and capabilities. May bob write the file using the group write bit?

options.A: No; mode 0460 denies reading to every user
options.B: Yes; owner and group permissions are always ORed together
options.C: No; the matching owner class grants bob read only
options.D: Yes; every owner automatically has all file data access rights

questions.explanation: The owner class applies when the user owns the file. The kernel does not fall back to the more permissive group class for that same access check.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A non-root user has write and search permissions on a directory and can search its ancestors. The directory has no sticky bit. Its regular file has mode 0444, and no ACLs, immutable flags, or mount restrictions apply. Can that user unlink the file?

options.A: Yes; but only if the file's executable bit is set
options.B: No; the file must grant write permission before it can be unlinked
options.C: Yes; the relevant deletion permissions are on the containing directory
options.D: No; a file with mode 0444 can never be deleted by any user

questions.explanation: Unlinking removes a directory entry. Write plus search permission on its parent governs this operation under the stated conditions, rather than the file's data-write bit.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Bash with GNU utilities, LC_ALL=C, and an initially empty writable working directory. All shown commands run successfully unless their exit status is explicitly examined. What exact lines are printed by the quoted find pattern?
questions.code_snippet:
mkdir nested
touch app.log error.txt nested/old.log nested/note.md
find . -type f -name '*.log' | sort
questions.explanation: Quoting prevents the shell from expanding *.log before find sees it. find recursively selects regular files with matching basenames; sort fixes the output order.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Bash with GNU utilities, LC_ALL=C, and an initially empty writable working directory. All shown commands run successfully unless their exit status is explicitly examined. What exact lines does case-insensitive, numbered grep print?
questions.code_snippet:
printf 'Error: disk
error: cpu
OK
' | grep -in '^error:'
questions.explanation: -i matches both capitalizations, -n prefixes original line numbers, and grep preserves the original matched text.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Bash with GNU utilities, LC_ALL=C, and an initially empty writable working directory. All shown commands run successfully unless their exit status is explicitly examined. What total does this awk filter print?
questions.code_snippet:
printf 'api 3
web 5
api 7
' | awk '$1 == "api" {sum += $2} END {print sum}'
questions.explanation: Only records whose first field is api contribute their second fields: 3+7=10.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Bash with GNU utilities, LC_ALL=C, and an initially empty writable working directory. All shown commands run successfully unless their exit status is explicitly examined. What exact lines are printed by this substitution without a g flag?
questions.code_snippet: printf 'red red\nblue red\n' | sed 's/red/green/'
questions.explanation: Without g, sed replaces only the first match on each line. It still processes every input line.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Bash with GNU utilities, LC_ALL=C, and an initially empty writable working directory. All shown commands run successfully unless their exit status is explicitly examined. What exact service-count lines are printed?
questions.code_snippet:
printf '200 api
500 db
503 api
404 web
' | awk '$1 >= 500 {print $2}' | sort | uniq -c | awk '{print $2, $1}'
questions.explanation: The first awk retains db and api for statuses at least 500. Sorting orders them as api,db; uniq counts one of each.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Bash with GNU utilities, LC_ALL=C, and an initially empty writable working directory. All shown commands run successfully unless their exit status is explicitly examined. What exact file contents are printed after overwrite followed by append?
questions.code_snippet:
printf 'first\n' > output.txt
printf 'second\n' >> output.txt
cat output.txt
questions.explanation: The first redirection creates or truncates the file. The second appends, preserving the first line.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Bash with GNU utilities, LC_ALL=C, and an initially empty writable working directory. All shown commands run successfully unless their exit status is explicitly examined. What exact lines are printed after both streams are redirected to the same file?
questions.explanation: stdout is first directed to combined.txt, then stderr duplicates that destination. The sequential writes therefore appear in the file as out then err.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Bash with GNU utilities, LC_ALL=C, and an initially empty writable working directory. All shown commands run successfully unless their exit status is explicitly examined. With pipefail disabled, what line count and pipeline exit status are printed? The grep intentionally finds no match.
questions.code_snippet:
set +o pipefail
printf 'alpha
beta
' | grep '^z' | wc -l
printf '%s
' "$?"
questions.explanation: grep returns 1 and sends no lines onward, so wc prints 0 and succeeds. Without pipefail, the pipeline status is the final command's status, zero.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Bash with GNU utilities, LC_ALL=C, and an initially empty writable working directory. All shown commands run successfully unless their exit status is explicitly examined. What exact per-service successful-duration totals are printed?
questions.code_snippet:
printf 'api,200,12
web,500,8
api,503,7
api,200,3
web,200,11
' | awk -F, '$2 >= 200 && $2 < 300 {sum[$1] += $3} END {for (key in sum) print key, sum[key]}' | sort
questions.explanation: The filter keeps only 2xx rows. api contributes 12+3=15 and web contributes 11. Sorting removes awk associative-iteration order from the result.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Bash with GNU utilities, LC_ALL=C, and an initially empty writable working directory. All shown commands run successfully unless their exit status is explicitly examined. What sum and record count remain after selecting every BEGIN-to-END block?
questions.code_snippet:
printf 'BEGIN
x=2
x=5
END
x=9
BEGIN
x=4
END
' | sed -n '/^BEGIN$/,/^END$/p' | awk -F= '/^x=/ {sum += $2; count++} END {print sum, count}'
questions.explanation: sed includes both marked blocks but excludes x=9 outside them. awk counts and sums only x records: 2,5,4 yield 11 across three records.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Bash with GNU utilities, LC_ALL=C, and an initially empty writable working directory. All shown commands run successfully unless their exit status is explicitly examined. What exact lines are printed when stderr is duplicated before stdout is redirected into saved.txt?
questions.explanation: The pipe is connected first. 2>&1 copies that pipe destination to stderr; the later > changes only stdout. E passes through sed, while O is saved and printed afterward.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Bash with GNU utilities, LC_ALL=C, and an initially empty writable working directory. All shown commands run successfully unless their exit status is explicitly examined. What line is selected after aggregating consecutive groups and sorting by their totals?
questions.code_snippet:
printf 'A 3
A 5
B 4
B 8
A 2
' | awk '$1 != previous {if (NR > 1) print previous, sum; previous = $1; sum = 0} {sum += $2} END {print previous, sum}' | sort -k2,2n | sed -n '2p'
questions.explanation: The awk program groups adjacent runs rather than all equal keys globally, producing A 8, B 12, A 2. Numeric sorting gives A 2, A 8, B 12, so line two is A 8.

questions.subpart_name: Linux / Unix OS Environment & Shell Commands
questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Assume ordinary Linux mode bits with no default ACLs or special bits. A program creates f with requested mode 0666 under umask 077. It then executes chmod g=u f and chmod u-x,g-w,o=r f. Next, umask changes to 027 and the program creates directory d with requested mode 0777. What are the final modes?
questions.explanation: Creation gives f=0600. Copying owner permissions to group gives 0660; removing owner execute has no effect, removing group write gives 0640, and assigning other read gives 0644. Directory creation under 027 gives 0750.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Under standard HTTP semantics, which method is both safe and idempotent for retrieving a resource representation?
questions.explanation: GET requests retrieval without asking for a state-changing action and is idempotent. DELETE is idempotent but not safe; POST and PATCH have no general idempotency guarantee.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A POST successfully creates a new resource, and the server can identify its URI. Which response most directly communicates creation?

options.A: 201 Created, normally with a Location header identifying the resource
options.B: 200 OK as a mandatory creation-only status
options.C: 404 Not Found with the new resource representation
options.D: 301 Moved Permanently as a creation acknowledgment

questions.explanation: 201 specifically indicates creation. Location can identify the primary new resource; 200 is a general success code rather than the creation-specific choice.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Which mapping of HTTP response status families is correct?
questions.explanation: HTTP assigns client errors to the 4xx class and server errors to the 5xx class. The classes describe response semantics, not which party must always change code.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A normal GET succeeds and returns the requested representation without a redirect or conditional-cache result. Which status is appropriate?
questions.explanation: 200 indicates successful processing; for GET, its content normally represents the target resource.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: An existing public page has moved permanently to a new URI, and the response supplies that URI in Location. Which listed status expresses that permanent redirect?
questions.explanation: 301 communicates a permanent URI change. 304 is a conditional-request result, not a redirect to a new page.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: The origin server has no current representation for a requested URI and chooses to report that absence. Which status fits?
questions.explanation: 404 reports that no current representation was found or that the server is unwilling to disclose one. This scenario explicitly reports absence.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: Which browser storage mechanism is automatically attached to eligible HTTP requests according to its scope, attributes, credentials mode, and browser policy?

options.C: All JavaScript variables in the page

questions.explanation: Browsers generate Cookie headers for eligible stored cookies. Web Storage and ordinary variables are not automatically serialized into HTTP requests.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A resource API supports complete replacement of a representation and partial modification of specified fields. Which method pairing best matches those intended operations?

options.A: POST is the only method capable of either operation
options.B: PUT for replacement; PATCH for partial modification
options.C: PATCH for complete replacement only; GET for partial modification
options.D: GET for replacement; DELETE for partial modification

questions.explanation: PUT expresses creation or replacement of target state using the supplied representation. PATCH applies a patch document. The precise accepted representations and patch format are API-defined.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: The first DELETE /items/7 removes an existing item and returns success. A repeated identical DELETE returns 404 because the item is already absent. Is that status difference alone a violation of DELETE idempotency?

options.A: No; the intended final state is still that item 7 is absent
options.B: Yes; idempotency requires identical status codes and bodies
options.C: No; because DELETE is defined as a safe read-only method
options.D: Yes; DELETE must recreate the item before a retry

questions.explanation: Idempotency concerns the intended effect on server state, not identical responses. Both requests leave the item absent, even if the second response differs.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: GET /accounts/7?close=true closes an account as its requested action. Which HTTP design issue is most direct?

options.A: It is correct solely because the URI uses a noun
options.B: It violates a rule that GET cannot contain a query string
options.C: It assigns a requested state-changing action to the safe GET method
options.D: It makes every response automatically uncacheable regardless of headers

questions.explanation: GET is intended to be safe. Query parameters are allowed, but using one to request account closure violates safe-method semantics and risks unintended activation by automated retrieval.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A client has a cached GET representation tagged "v3". It sends If-None-Match: "v3", and the selected current representation still matches that validator. What response normally allows reuse of the cached representation?

options.A: 301 Moved Permanently with a new URI required
options.C: 500 Internal Server Error because the validator matched
options.D: 304 Not Modified, without a response content body

questions.explanation: For a conditional GET, a matching If-None-Match validator leads to 304. The client reuses its stored representation; the 304 does not carry a replacement representation body.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A server rejects an HTTP request because its request syntax is malformed. Which listed status is the direct client-error choice?
questions.explanation: 400 covers malformed syntax and other perceived client-request errors. 401 concerns authentication, while 503 signals temporary service unavailability.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
questions.question: A protected endpoint receives no acceptable authentication credentials and challenges the client to authenticate. Which response pairing fits standard HTTP semantics?

options.A: 403 Forbidden with a mandatory Location redirect
options.C: 200 OK with a mandatory WWW-Authenticate challenge
options.D: 502 Bad Gateway with a session identifier

questions.explanation: 401 indicates the absence of valid authentication credentials for the target resource. The server must include at least one applicable WWW-Authenticate challenge.

questions.module: Module 4: Applied Systems, Cloud & Software Engineering
